extracted.intended_audience: organizations and practitioners who publish nonpartisan fact-checks (fact-checking newsrooms and related organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: A short code setting ethical and procedural commitments for organizations that regularly publish nonpartisan accuracy reports about public figures, institutions, and widely circulated claims. Specifies standards on impartiality, transparency, methodology, corrections, and organizational disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: target activity and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: This code of principles is for organizations that regularly publish nonpartisan reports on the accuracy of statements by public figures, major institutions, and other widely circulated claims of interest to society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the result of consultations among fact-checkers from around the world and offers conscientious practitioners principles to aspire to in their everyday work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisanship and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations fact-check claims using the same standard for every fact check and do not concentrate their fact-checking on any one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They follow the same process for every fact check and let the evidence dictate the conclusions. Signatories do not advocate or take policy positions on the issues they fact-check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories provide all sources in enough detail that readers can replicate their work, except where a source's personal security could be compromised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases where personal security could be compromised, signatories provide as much detail as possible so readers can still verify findings themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Funding & Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations are transparent about their funding sources and organizational details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they accept funding from other organizations, they ensure that funders have no influence over the conclusions the fact-checkers reach. Signatory organizations detail the professional background of all key figures in the organization and explain the organizational structure and legal status. Signatories clearly indicate a way for readers to communicate with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories explain the methodology they use to select, research, write, edit, publish and correct their fact checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They encourage readers to send claims to fact-check and are transparent on why and how they fact-check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open & Honest Corrections Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories publish their corrections policy and follow it scrupulously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They correct clearly and transparently in line with the corrections policy, seeking so far as possible to ensure that readers see the corrected version.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFCN badge usage and signatory listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations that have obtained IFCN verification are encouraged to publish a badge on their homepage; the complete list of signatories is maintained publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any organization that holds the IFCN badge but is not listed is NOT a signatory to the code of principles.
